title: Concurrency
theory:
> **Curriculum:** This chapter follows [LEARN-LANGUAGES/CURRICULUM.md](../../CURRICULUM.md). Exercise ids are shared across LEARN-* repos for cross-reference.

## Threads

`Thread`, `ExecutorService`, and joining tasks for deterministic stdout.

exercises.title: Goroutine
exercises.description: Launch Java sayHello(). Print main done. Use time.Sleep to let Javaroutine run.

exercises.title: Channel
exercises.description: Create ch := make(chan string). Send "ping" to ch in Javaroutine, receive and print.

exercises.title: Buffered Channel
exercises.description: Create a buffered channel with capacity 2. Send 10 and 20 without blocking. Then receive and print both.

exercises.title: Select Statement
exercises.description: Create two channels ch1 and ch2. Send to ch1 in Javaroutine after 10ms. Use select to receive whichever comes first.

exercises.title: Channel Close
exercises.description: Create channel, send 1,2,3 then close. Use range to receive until closed.
hints: for n := range ch prints until closed

exercises.title: Fan-In Pattern
exercises.description: Create two Javaroutines that each send a string to a shared channel. Use a third Javaroutine to fan-in (read) from the channel and print received values. Close the channel when both senders are done.
hints: Use wg.Add(2) for the two sender goroutines
In a third goroutine, defer close(ch) after wg.Wait()
Range over ch to collect all values

exercises.title: WaitGroup
exercises.description: Use sync.WaitGroup to launch 3 Javaroutines that each print their number, then wait for all to complete before printing "done".
